decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark — Paste a web address”; round 1 client did not contest URL-based saving.
decisions.note: Conforming baseline specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “open links in a new tab”; round 1 client did not contest this behavior.
decisions.note: Opening the original URL conforms at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Tag bookmarks and filter the list by tag”; round 1 client retained tags and requested only additional tag behavior.
decisions.note: Assignment and single-tag filtering conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Edit & delete … delete with a confirmation step”; round 1 client did not reject deletion.
decisions.note: Deletion is present; confirmation is additional to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only promises “See all bookmarks” and does not expose the required title, description, tags, and favicon per item. Round 1 client does not mention list-card contents; the expectation appears only in round 2: “The normal bookmark list should show the description alongside the title, tags, and favicon.”
decisions.note: Initial specification-gate list presentation omits required readability fields and passes that response unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “No automatic page-metadata fetching”; round 1 client: “Saving a link should automatically collect its title, description, favicon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: Client rejects an explicit contradiction at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limits saving to an “optional title/tags” and says titles are typed or URL-derived; round 1 client adds: “I should be able to edit the title and description.”
decisions.note: Client supplies the missing editable metadata behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker merely lists “duplicates” among edge cases without the required convergence behavior; round 1 client specifies: “take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it, never offer to create a duplicate.”
decisions.note: Client supplies the reference-conforming duplicate rule at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set has no notes; round 1 client: “support a personal note, including formatted Markdown.”
decisions.note: Missing extended requirement is added.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers only “search by keyword”; round 1 client specifies search over “title, description, note, and address.”
decisions.note: Client extends underspecified keyword search to all required fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker does not state case behavior; round 1 client requires search to “be case-insensitive.”
decisions.note: Missing search rule is supplied.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents generic keyword search; round 1 client requests “`#tag` searches.”
decisions.note: Missing tag-search syntax is added.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents generic keyword search; round 1 client requests “combinations using AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: Missing Boolean search grammar is added.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents generic keyword search; round 1 client requests “exact quoted phrases.”
decisions.note: Missing exact-phrase behavior is added.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offers tags but no suggestions; round 1 client: “Existing tags should be suggested while I type.”
decisions.note: Autocomplete is added at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set omits read-later state; round 1 client: “I need a read-later state.”
decisions.note: Client adds explicit unread marking.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set omits an unread perspective; round 1 client requests “a separate unread view.”
decisions.note: Client adds the missing unread list.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set omits read-state transitions; round 1 client requests “a way to mark items read.”
decisions.note: Client adds the missing read action.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 browse story has no sorting; round 1 client: “I need sorting.”
decisions.note: Client adds list sorting.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set has no multi-selection; round 1 client requests “selecting multiple bookmarks for actions such as changing tags, marking read/unread, archiving, or deleting.”
decisions.note: Client adds selected-item bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set has no view-wide action; round 1 client says the actions “should be usable for all results in the current filtered view.”
decisions.note: Client adds filter-scoped whole-collection actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set omits archiving; round 1 client requires archived links to “disappear from the normal list and search.”
decisions.note: Client adds archive behavior and default-search exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 has deletion but no archive distinction; round 1 client: “Archiving must be separate from deletion” and archived items must be restorable.
decisions.note: Client adds reversible archive semantics distinct from permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 has no archive view; round 1 client says archived links must “remain available in their own view.”
decisions.note: Client adds the separate archived list.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set omits bundles; round 1 client requests “saved reusable views that combine a search with included or excluded tags.”
decisions.note: Client adds saved dynamic filters.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly assumes “No browser bookmark import/export”; round 1 client: “I do want browser bookmark import … preserving titles, tags, and original dates.”
decisions.note: Client rejects the import exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly assumes “No browser bookmark import/export”; round 1 client: “I do want browser bookmark … export.”
decisions.note: Client rejects the export exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set has no preservation; round 1 client requests each page as “a local snapshot, with PDFs saved as PDFs.”
decisions.note: Client adds local snapshotting and the PDF rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set has no external archival action; round 1 client requests “an option to save it through the Internet Archive.”
decisions.note: Client adds Internet Archive support.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 feature set omits preferences; round 1 client requests “default sorting, number of items shown, and font size.”
decisions.note: Client adds display settings.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Auto-collect title, description, favicon, preview; edit title & description.”
decisions.note: Revised specification now conforms for metadata collection and metadata editing.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Duplicate address → go to existing bookmark, never duplicate”; round 2 client says the proposed duplicate matching “sound[s] right.”
decisions.note: Revised duplicate behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Personal note in Markdown”; round 2 client does not contest it.
decisions.note: Revised note behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents search over all four fields, case-insensitive matching, `#tag`, quoted phrases, and AND/OR/NOT with parentheses.
decisions.note: The listed baseline search capabilities conform; narrower semantic omissions are classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Suggest existing tags while typing.”
decisions.note: Revised autocomplete decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Read-later state + separate unread view + mark read.”
decisions.note: The core read-later lifecycle is present; the incorrect initial default is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker explicitly includes “Sorting.”
decisions.note: Revised sorting decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “multi-select bulk actions; same actions on whole filtered view.”
decisions.note: Selection and filter-scoped action coverage conform; add/remove tag specificity is classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Archive separate from delete; own view; restorable.”
decisions.note: Revised archive lifecycle conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “Saved reusable views (search + included/excluded tags).”
decisions.note: Revised bundle decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents browser HTML import/export preserving titles, tags, and original dates; round 2 client says the format “sound[s] right.”
decisions.note: Revised import/export decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker retains the “Internet Archive option”; round 2 client accepts graceful external-service failure.
decisions.note: Internet Archive support conforms; failure-visibility preference is outside the reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents “default sort, items shown, font size.”
decisions.note: Revised display-preference decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: The round 2 specification treated new bookmarks as unread, confirmed by round 3 maker’s change summary: “New bookmarks not auto-unread.” Round 2 client rejects this: “New bookmarks should not automatically be unread. Let me deliberately mark a bookmark as ‘read later.’”
decisions.note: Client rejects the incorrect default at the second specification review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker only calls out editing title and description; round 2 client requires editing “the bookmark’s address as well as its title, description, tags, and note.”
decisions.note: Client adds the missing complete edit-field set.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 revised presentation does not state that descriptions appear in the normal list; round 2 client requires “description alongside the title, tags, and favicon.”
decisions.note: Client catches the still-incomplete list presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker lists keyword and `#tag` capabilities without their combination rule; round 2 client specifies that both “should both have to match unless I explicitly use OR.”
decisions.note: Client supplies the required implicit-AND semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation does not make operator case behavior explicit; round 2 client: “AND, OR, and NOT should work regardless of capitalization.”
decisions.note: Client corrects Boolean operator case handling.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 presentation lists quoted phrases and operators but omits the quoted-operator rule; round 2 client says an operator inside quotes “should be searched as ordinary text.”
decisions.note: Client supplies the required literal-treatment rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says only “changing tags”; round 2 client requires bulk tag changes to “explicitly support both adding and removing tags.”
decisions.note: Client adds the missing two-way bulk-tag behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents only “Local snapshots, PDFs as PDFs”; round 2 response does not require a single self-contained HTML file. Round 5 maker later confirms the specification was changed so FR-038 “now requires” one self-contained HTML file.
decisions.note: The revised specification still omitted the reference’s single-file rule, and that round’s response did not surface it.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “New bookmarks not auto-unread; you set ‘read later’ deliberately and toggle”; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected read-state decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: editing includes “address … title, description, tags, note”; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected complete-edit decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: normal list shows “description alongside title, tags, favicon”; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected list-content decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “Keyword + `#tag` together ⇒ both must match unless explicit `OR`”; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected implicit-AND behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “AND/OR/NOT case-insensitive; quoted ⇒ literal text”; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected Boolean and quoted-operator semantics conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “Bulk tag change explicitly supports add and remove”; round 3 client approves.
decisions.note: Corrected bulk-tag decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker describes “a self-contained copy of each page” but does not commit to the required single-file form; round 4 client requires “a self-contained, single HTML file … without fetching assets,” with PDFs preserved.
decisions.note: Client catches the single-file snapshot omission at the implementation-plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker commits to “one `.html` with CSS inlined, images/fonts embedded as `data:` URIs,” offline with no source callbacks, and PDFs kept as PDFs; round 5 client explicitly approves “genuinely self-contained snapshots.”
decisions.note: Corrected snapshot plan conforms.
